subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - postcall recap
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir@finlytics.ai>, Procurement <procurement@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - postcall recap

Hi Samir + team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good conversation and appreciate you walking us through the current production profile. TL;DR from our side and proposed next steps below.

Key requirements you mentioned on the call:
- End-to-end p95 latency target: <= 300ms (goal you mentioned: 250ms)
- End-to-end p99 latency target: <= 600ms (goal you mentioned: 450ms)
- Target sustained throughput: ~400 QPS for short-chat / API traffic (peak bursts to 1.5x)
- Concurrency: steady ~60, occasional spot bursts up to ~200 for <60s
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming is required for the new chat UI (SSE/Websocket)
- Workload characteristics: median request tokens ~120, responses avg ~60 tokens; some long-form outliers to 1k tokens

Current provider (as discussed): you reported observable p95/p99 tail latency that is above your targets, particularly for p99 (you mentioned seeing p99 ~1s+ under load).

What Redwood delivered on the call:
- High-level hosted API numbers (non-binding): p95 ~220ms, p99 ~380ms for comparable short-chat profile (single-region, token-streaming enabled)
- Support for streaming (SSE) with first-byte and trailing token delivery, and options to tune chunking/buffer sizes
- Autoscaling + reserved capacity options to handle burst concurrency without tail spikes

Action items / next steps (proposed):
1) Redwood to share a short SLO comparison pack and sample benchmark traces (attached: redwood-slo-comparison.pdf).
2) Finlytics to confirm final p95/p99 targets (you mentioned 250/450 as ideal).
3) Schedule a tech deep-dive with your infra/observability folks to review traces and telemetry we can collect (requesting sample traces/end-to-end request ids).
4) Redwood to run a targeted benchmark that mirrors your median/peak token distribution and the streaming pattern (Marissa will own).
5) Procurement: initial timeline/PO questions — if we can get an expected procurement window that helps prioritize Dedicated capacity planning.

Attachments: redwood-slo-comparison.pdf, finlytics-action-items.xlsx

Happy to set up the deep-dive — proposing Wed or Thu next week.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Samir Desai <samir@finlytics.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finlytics.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - postcall recap

Thanks Laura — great summary. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Our ideal targets are p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms end-to-end (these are user-facing targets for chat latency).
- Sustained throughput is roughly 350-450 QPS for our primary region (US-W), with burst patterns tied to product launches (bursts up to ~2000 QPS for ~30s seen historically).
- Concurrency: steady-state concurrency of ~80 connections, but we commonly see short spikes to ~200 concurrent streams. Maintaining tail behavior during those spikes is critical.
- Streaming is required; we stream tokens to the client and rely on timely first-byte to show typing indicator.
- Current provider: CloudServe — our observed numbers under realistic load are p95 ~480ms, p99 ~1.1s. We want to get back under our target with minimal UX regressions.

What we'd like from Redwood next:
1) Sample end-to-end traces and span breakdown (network, queuing, model, tokenization) so our SREs can validate.
2) A benchmarking plan that includes streaming tests and sustained-burst patterns (we can provide a short workload replay).
3) High-level SLA language on latency objectives and remediation options for missed SLOs (we'll want to see draft SLA language).

I'll loop in procurement separately with expected timeline (targeting Q3 purchase).

Best,
Samir
Samir Desai
Head of Platform, Finlytics
samir@finlytics.ai
+1 (212) 555-0133

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@finlytics.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - postcall recap

Thanks Samir — this is super helpful and matches what we heard. Quick responses inline and next steps: 

- Targets: we can commit to validating a configuration that meets your ideal targets (p95 250ms / p99 450ms) in our hosted environment using the benchmark trace you provide. Final guarantees would be part of SLA and Dedicated capacity planning.
- Bursts: we'll include sustained-burst scenarios and concurrency spikes in the benchmark (including short 30s spikes to ~2000 QPS) and measure tail behavior.
- Streaming: our hosted API supports token-by-token SSE and websocket streaming. We'll test first-byte latency and chunking to match your UI expectations.
- Traces & telemetry: attaching a short draft SLA + guidance on the trace/span format we'll collect (SLA-draft-Redwood-Finlytics.pdf). We can accept telemetry in OpenTelemetry span format or simple request/response logs with request ids.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
1) You share a short workload replay and any representative trace ids (by EOD Tue) — we can also accept a Postman/locust script.
2) Redwood runs benchmark (Marissa) and returns a perf report with p50/p95/p99 and tail breakdowns within 5 business days after we receive the replay.
3) Tech deep-dive to go over traces and proposed config (30-45m) — propose Thu next week (please confirm availability).
4) Procurement: Laura to sync with Samir separately; initial SLA draft attached.

Marissa — can you pick this up once Samir shares the replay? We'll run the short benchmark in our hosted environment and then repeat on a Dedicated config if needed.

Laura

Attachment: SLA-draft-Redwood-Finlytics.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - postcall recap

Got it — I'll own the benchmarking plan. Plan summary:
- Recreate Finlytics token distribution (median req 120 tokens / resp 60 tokens) and streaming behavior.
- Run hosted baseline first (3 x 30-min runs, steady-state + burst phases) capturing p50/p95/p99 and per-stage spans.
- If hosted baseline misses targets, spin a Dedicated config (pinned capacity + prewarm) and repeat.
- Deliverables: bench report, raw traces (OTel), and a short recommendation (config + estimated cost delta).

I'll start once Samir shares the replay or sample traces. Target delivery: 5 business days after artifacts received.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
SRE, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
